tagline: A shoreline route through Grayton Beach, Seaside and protected coastal land
intro: County Road 30A leaves US 98 west of Santa Rosa Beach and turns southeast toward the Gulf of Mexico. It follows the shoreline through Grayton Beach and Seaside, crossing parts of Point Washington State Forest and Deer Lake State Park. At its western end, the road separates the state forest from Topsail Hill Preserve State Park. At Grayton Beach State Park, the landscape includes salt marshes and dunes covered in sea oats, with Western Lake among the dune lakes visible from the road.

In 1913, W. H. Butler and his son Van R. Butler took a full day to travel from DeFuniak Springs to Grayton Beach. Access to this coast changed in the early 1930s with the completion of Highway 98, the Highway 331 bridge and the Intracoastal Waterway through Walton County. Those connections made Grayton Beach and South Walton easier to reach. Seaside’s construction began in 1981, following Robert S. Davis’s plan for a beach town of traditional wood-framed cottages.
Traveling east, the route reaches Grayton Beach before Seaside. Beyond Seaside, the road crosses Deer Lake State Park southeast of Seagrove Beach, then rejoins US 98 near Inlet Beach.

moments.title: Grayton Beach
moments.text: Grayton Beach sits in the middle of a twenty-mile stretch of coastal dune lakes, with Western Lake nearby. The Coastal Heritage Preservation Foundation dates Army major Charles T. Gray’s settlement here to 1885. William Miller and William Wilson arrived in 1890, laid out streets and blocks, and named the village for Gray. Most land north of County Road 30A in the community is now state park. The adjoining Grayton Beach State Park includes salt marshes and dunes covered with sea oats. The park opened in 1968 on land obtained through a 1964 lease from the Florida Board of Education.

moments.title: Seaside
moments.text: Seaside began with a plan to build an old-fashioned beach town. After inheriting the land in 1978, Robert S. Davis, his wife Daryl and architects Andrés Duany and Elizabeth Plater-Zyberk studied southern towns as models. Construction began in 1981. Its New Urbanism principles promote walkability and mixed uses. The town became the set for The Truman Show in 1998. Individual houses must differ from one another; front yards use native plants and have no private front lawns. Because the development was privately owned, its developers could write the zoning codes that governed its design.
moments.notice: Front yards use native plants, with no private front lawns.

moments.title: Deer Lake State Park
moments.text: Deer Lake State Park occupies a stretch of the 30A corridor southeast of Seagrove Beach. The road crosses three miles of the park. Its recreational amenities include beaches, birding, fishing and wildlife viewing. Grayton Beach State Recreation Area is its sister park.
